game: DET@PHI Week 11 2025, kickoff 2025-11-16 20:20 ET, outdoor, PHI -2.5, total 46.5

script.base: Short home favorite in a moderate 46.5 game: implied PHI 24.5, DET 22.0, spread only 2.5 so this is competitive into the fourth quarter, not a blowout, and starters should play full snaps. PHI leans on Saquon Barkley late if they hold the lead (54 carries, 254 yards over weeks 7/8/10); DET stays in a Gibbs/Montgomery split (41 and 39 carries) while Jared Goff still has to throw, with Sam LaPorta out.
script.flip1: PHI scores early and leads by 10+ at half. Barkley and Jalen Hurts run the clock, Jahmyr Gibbs and David Montgomery rush yards stall as DET abandons the run, and DET target volume shifts to Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams while Devonta Smith's second-half routes shrink.
script.flip2: DET controls the trenches and leads late. PHI throws to catch up, so Barkley carries die and Smith/A.J. Brown/Dallas Goedert targets rise; Williams's vertical shots get taken away if DET is protecting a lead and Gibbs/Montgomery just run clock.

injury_fallout: DET TE Sam LaPorta is out (back; 16 targets, 165 yards, 84 air over weeks 7/9/10). Brock Wright is questionable, so that share is more likely to hit St. Brown (31 targets), Jameson Williams (15), Gibbs (10) and Kalif Raymond (8) than a backup TE. DET tackles Taylor Decker (shoulder) and Penei Sewell (ankle) are questionable and G Miles Frazier is out, so if the tackles sit Goff's deep shots (Williams) are the losers and quick throws to RBs go up. DET defense is gutted for PHI skill players: S Kerby Joseph out, CB Terrion Arnold out, CB D.J. Reed out, CB Amik Robertson questionable, LB Malcolm Rodriguez out, DEs Marcus Davenport and Joshua Paschal out. That missing secondary/LB group is the gain for Devonta Smith first, then Brown and Goedert, with a lesser run-game bump for Barkley. PHI only lists C Willie Lampkin questionable; no PHI skill-player out. Isaac TeSlaa, Jacob Saylors and Sione Vaki questionable are depth, not usage changers. Sources: pack official injury report and the weeks 7-10 target/carry lines. Final inactives (~90 min pre-kick) are not in the pack.

matchup.shell: No coverage charting, MOFO/MOFC or man/zone rates in the pack. Location splits are the shell proxy: PHI allows left 6.79 YPA (109 att), middle 5.61 (62), right 6.91 (129); DET allows left 7.07 (107), middle 9.29 (62), right 5.63 (116). DET's middle is the structural hole; PHI is softer outside than in the middle.
matchup.pressure: PHI blitzes 28%; DET EPA/dropback is 0.51 vs blitz and 0.15 vs none, so Goff is better, not worse, when pressured and a moderate blitz does not kill DET explosives. DET blitzes 32%; PHI EPA/dropback is 0.08 vs blitz and 0.18 vs none, so Hurts is the QB who gets sped up. DET edge Davenport and Paschal are out, which can lower DET's pressure even at a 32% blitz rate. Decker/Sewell questionable is the DET pass-protection risk.
matchup.bleeds: DET bleeds the middle (9.29 YPA on 62 throws) and has also allowed 26 passes of 20+ for 315 yards in 9 games; rush defense is ordinary (4.33 YPC, 25 runs of 10+). PHI rush defense is ordinary (4.46 YPC, 29 runs of 10+) and the pass bleed is the outside (6.79/6.91), not the middle (5.61). Both defenses have 26 explosives of 20+.
matchup.overlap: PHI's primary is Devonta Smith (27 targets, 336 yards, 368 air in the three-game window, about 13.6 aDOT) into DET's missing Joseph/Arnold/Reed and the 9.29 middle YPA. That is the clean overlap. DET's primary St. Brown (31 targets, 269 air, about 8.7 aDOT) maps toward PHI's best zone, the middle at 5.61, not the soft outside. Williams (15 targets, 172 air, about 11.5 aDOT) is the DET player who actually attacks PHI's outside weakness, and LaPorta being out is the usage overlap.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both overs lost. PHI led by two scores at half, Barkley topped 20 second-half carries, Hurts threw under 25 times, and Smith finished in the 49-yard neighborhood while the 9.29 middle YPA turned out to be 62 throws of noise rather than a corner Smith actually lines up against. On the other side the zero came back: PHI kept two safeties deep, St. Brown took the LaPorta targets (he already had 31), Gibbs took the checkdowns (10 targets, -14 air), and Williams never saw a catchable vertical. If Decker and Sewell were inactive, the 28% blitz got home anyway and the 172 air yards never left the pocket. The median stand-ins were never a soft market, just each player's own 50th percentile, and without a no-vig there was no proof the number was wrong.
slip_story: One story only: competitive pass volume in a 46.5 game with both teams in the low-20s, not a clock-kill and not a slog. Smith over and Williams over win together if both quarterbacks throw and lose together if PHI grinds with Barkley and DET sits on Gibbs/Montgomery. Do not add Barkley or Gibbs rush overs, a total under, or any TD. Two legs, one market per player, no depth-receiver legs. Not a bet: no price, no sim gate.
